tasks.instruction: Pytania wlasne do mapy mysli OJAJ 2026/27 o Wielkiej Brytanii (nie z arkusza olimpiady). Z podanych odpowiedzi wybierz poprawna. Tylko jedna jest prawidlowa.

items.stem: What are the three components of the UK Parliament?
options: A) the House of Commons, the House of Lords and the Prime Minister
B) the House of Commons, the Supreme Court and the monarch
C) the House of Commons, the House of Lords and the monarch
D) the Cabinet, the House of Lords and the Prime Minister

items.stem: How many Members of Parliament (MPs) sit in the House of Commons?
How do most members of the House of Lords get their seats?
options: A) They are elected every five years.
B) They all inherit their seats from their fathers.
C) They are chosen by lot from ordinary citizens.
D) They are appointed, not elected.

items.stem: What is one of the jobs of the Serjeant at Arms?
options: A) writing the monarch's speech
B) keeping order in the House of Commons and carrying the Mace
C) counting the votes in general elections
D) choosing the Prime Minister

items.stem: What happens when Black Rod comes to call MPs to the State Opening of Parliament?
options: A) Black Rod reads the monarch's speech in the House of Commons.
B) The door of the Commons is slammed shut, and Black Rod knocks on it three times.
C) MPs throw their order papers at Black Rod.
D) Black Rod locks the MPs inside until the ceremony is over.

items.stem: Why is the official sometimes called "Lady Usher of the Black Rod"?
options: A) The post was created for a queen.
B) The job has always been done by a woman.
C) It is the title used only in the House of Commons.
D) Since 2018 the post has been held by a woman.

items.stem: What does the Mace in the House of Commons represent?
options: A) the authority of the monarch, without which the House cannot meet or pass laws
B) the power of the Prime Minister over the Cabinet
C) the victory of Parliament in the Falklands War
D) the right of MPs to carry weapons
A) the bag in which MPs' votes are collected
B) the Speaker's chair in the House of Commons
C) the seat of the Lord Speaker in the House of Lords
D) the monarch's throne in Westminster Abbey

items.stem: What does the monarch do at the State Opening of Parliament?
options: A) chooses the new Speaker of the House of Commons
B) votes on the first new law of the year
C) opens the doors of the House of Commons in person
D) reads a speech, written by the government, setting out its plans

items.stem: What is devolution in the UK?
options: A) the system in which the monarch chooses the Prime Minister
B) passing some powers from the UK Parliament to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
C) the gradual change of the Labour Party into the Conservative Party
D) the division of London into boroughs
